text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski opened talks with President Arpad Goncz and Premier Gyula Horn on issues related to the two countries' planned accession to the EU and NATO. @

- Leaders of the two coalition parties continue to be divided over the privatisation law amendment sent back by President Arpad Goncz to Parliament, but agreed at a meeting of the coalition consultative council on Monday on the need to have Parliament pass on the rejected conflict of interest bill and on continuing the constitutional process.

- Parliament's immunity committee will recommend that the legislature waive the immunity right of Socialist MP and treasurer Laszlo Boldvai. The prosecutor general wants to charge Boldvai with abuse of influence in connection with the transfer of large sums of money from lawyer Marta Tocsik. @

- The Democratic Forum is seeking to put forward a no-confidence motion to Parliament against Prime Minister Gyula Horn and his cabinet primarily because of the latest developments in the Tocsik scandal.

- The Prime Minister's experts on the Gabcikovo hydropower plant, state secretary Janos Nemcsok and senior diplomatic adviser Tamas Horvath, dismissed rumours related to the construction of a hydropower plant at Esztergom as groundless.
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze said that the government must help settle the HUF 3 billion debt piled up by the police. @
- Yesterday's general meeting of the health insurance authority elected Laszlo Halmy its president.

- Magyar Hitel Bank's capital will skyrocket from HUF 7.14 billion to HUF 29.4 billion, following a decision at the general meeting. Dutch bank ABN Amro, which owns 89 percent of MHB, also reshuffled the entire management.

- Some HUF 2.6 billion worth of shares in the Budapest power plant Elmu were subscribed for by unauthorised persons who did not have enough compensation coupons to buy the shares, the State Securities Supervision announced. @
- The traditional paprika processing company Szegedi Paprika will be liquidated.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Federico Mayor, director general of Unesco, is due to arrive in Budapest for official talks today.
- Despite complaints by car sellers, the number of new cars bought by Hungarians increased to 75,000 last year up from 69,000 in 1995, said Hungarian Car Importers Association president Gabor Gyozo.
VILAGGAZDASAG @
- About 11 million tons of grain were grown in Hungary last year, 1 percent more than in 1995. The total amount of cereals was only 3.9 million tons, 15 percent below the 1995 amount.
- The German clutch manufacturer Lamellen- und Kupplungsbau GmbH has begun the construction of their factory in Szombathely.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The equity of OMV Kft., the subsidiary of the Austrian petrol company, increased to HUF 8.4 billion last year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- The redundancy package offered by the American firm AES Summit to workers at the Tiszai Eromu power plant has proven too tempting. Some 1,300 of the 2,000 employees at the Lyuko mine want to leave, the remaining staff may not be enough to operate the mine.
- Officials of Butler Manufacturing, the US construction giant, are finalising construction plans of their plant to be built in Nyiregyhaza.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
